the actions of pentobarbitone on sensory inflow to the thalamus via the spinothalomic tract is mediated by the mesopontine area.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the MPTA is a critical brain stem site where the actions of general anesthetics can be studied in awake animals and where the actions of these agents on sensory inflow to the thalamus can be investigated.
the MPTA is a key site for the actions of general anesthetics and that the MPTAs actions may involve the attenuation of sensory inflow through ascending sensory pathways.
the mesopontine anesthesia area is a key structure for general anesthesia and the barbiturates are a key drug for general anesthesia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MPTA is a site of action for barbiturate-induced general anesthesia.
the MPTA is a critical brain stem site for general anesthetic-induced antinociceptive effects.
the MPTA may be a useful model for studying the cellular mechanisms underlying the actions of general anesthetics.
